checks: For fixed pi, nonnegative weights and independent menu choices justify separation of minima across colors. The two minima commute, and the signed unit ball evaluates a covector to minus its dual norm at its minimum.

Compactness yields attained selections and extrema; uniform continuity makes the optimized inner values continuous in pi. A zero-radius weighted Minkowski sum is the singleton zero, and varying one positively weighted summand forces its menu to be a singleton.
Varying only menu p gives diameter at least pi_p D_p, and the maximal norm is at least half the diameter. Summing pi_p <= max_q(pi_q D_q)/D_p gives the displayed bound.

The centered interval sum has radius r for every weight and center a(2t-1). The best frozen weight is 1/2, while every transversal balances. The cone variant is exactly the dual cone inclusion, including the nonsingleton one-sided example.
Matched original §§2–3 and §7; archived checks of the game and related examples passed with exact rational/symbolic arithmetic.

overlap.comparison: Proves universal existence of a balance for each selected circuit collection. It does not freeze a single weight before all selections or give the norm gap and singleton characterization.

review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The two commuting minima give the exact negative dual-norm value, and the diameter and singleton tests quantify the additional demand made by a common weight vector.
